page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. System memory consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results show a contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the top tier (top 10%), as are single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the average tier (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests, including cached small block reads and uncached large block reads and writes, consistently register in the average tier. For LLM inference, text generation using a small 135M model achieves top-tier performance, whereas prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers dedicated AMD EPYC resources and local NVMe storage without the premium of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware classes. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core performance make it suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, database operations, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks. It is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compute or larger LLM inference workloads due to the observed performance drop-offs in those benchmarks.
description: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is a general-purpose server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, a 480 GB NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and small-model LLM text generation. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the average tier, while medium-model LLM prompt processing is weak. This hardware profile provides a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and database operations, offering a qualitative balance between dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and local NVMe storage.
